title: Chapter 12 Quiz
description: Test your understanding of the ML pipeline, capstone planning, and next steps in your machine learning journey!

questions.question: What is the correct order of steps in a typical ML project?
options: Model selection → EDA → deployment → data collection
Data collection → EDA → preprocessing → model training → evaluation → deployment
questions.explanation: You collect data, explore, preprocess, then train and evaluate before deploying.

questions.question: Which step involves creating new features from existing ones?
questions.explanation: Feature engineering transforms raw data into more informative inputs for the model.

questions.question: Why is a baseline model important?
options: It provides a simple benchmark to see if complex models add value
It replaces the need for a test set
questions.explanation: Baselines (e.g., majority class, linear regression) show the minimum performance to beat.

questions.question: Which metric is most appropriate for a cancer detection model where missing a positive case is extremely costly?
questions.explanation: High recall ensures that most actual positive cases are detected, which is critical in medical diagnosis.

questions.question: You are building a capstone project. What should you do first after choosing a dataset?
options: Jump straight into training a neural network
Explore and clean the data, then define a detailed plan
questions.explanation: A plan with EDA and preprocessing steps sets you up for success.

questions.question: Cross‑validation can be used to evaluate models without a separate test set.
questions.explanation: True. Cross‑validation provides a robust performance estimate, but a final hold‑out set is still recommended for reporting.

questions.question: What is data leakage?
options: Information from outside the training set accidentally used to create the model
questions.explanation: Data leakage occurs when the model has access to information it shouldn't during training, inflating performance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good practice when scaling features?
options: Scale all data together, then split
Fit scaler on training data, then transform both training and test
Never scale features for tree‑based models
questions.explanation: Fitting on training and transforming both prevents test data from influencing the scaling parameters.

questions.question: You finish your capstone. What should the final deliverable include?
options: A clear report with problem, approach, results, and insights
A single Python script without comments
questions.explanation: A well‑documented report tells the story of your work, which is crucial for portfolio and communication.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of MLOps?
options: To streamline the deployment, monitoring, and lifecycle management of ML models
questions.explanation: MLOps combines ML, DevOps, and data engineering to operationalize models reliably.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of concept drift?
options: Input features have different statistics than training
The relationship between features and target has changed
The model file size has increased
questions.explanation: Concept drift means the pattern the model learned no longer holds, even if features look similar.

questions.question: To showcase your skills to employers, what is most effective?
options: A GitHub portfolio with end‑to‑end projects
questions.explanation: Projects demonstrate applied skills and problem‑solving ability.

questions.question: Which advanced topic deals with models that create new data samples?
questions.explanation: Generative models learn to produce new data similar to the training distribution.

questions.question: What does SHAP help with?
options: Explaining individual predictions by attributing contributions to features
questions.explanation: SHAP provides interpretable feature attributions for any model.

questions.question: Which resource is a popular book for hands‑on ML with Python?
options: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy
Hands‑On Machine Learning with Scikit‑Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow (Aurélien Géron)
questions.explanation: Géron’s book is a widely recommended practical guide.

questions.question: Building a single well‑documented project is less valuable than completing many courses without applying the knowledge.
questions.explanation: False. Applied projects prove you can solve real problems, which is far more valuable.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for handling imbalanced classes in a capstone classification project?
options: Use metrics like precision, recall, F1, AUC, and consider resampling or class weights
Collect more data of the minority class only
questions.explanation: Imbalanced data requires careful metric selection and often resampling or weighted loss.

questions.question: In which phase would you use `GridSearchCV`?
questions.explanation: GridSearchCV searches hyperparameter space to find the best configuration.

questions.question: You want to continuously improve a deployed model. What pipeline component is essential?
options: A retraining pipeline triggered by performance degradation
questions.explanation: Automated retraining pipelines keep models fresh as data evolves.

questions.question: What is the most valuable outcome of this entire course?
options: Developing the ability to independently tackle a real‑world ML problem from start to finish
questions.explanation: The ultimate goal is confident, independent problem‑solving using the complete ML toolkit.
